title: The Toll of the Canopy Hoarder
story: A great sloth-beast has stolen all the rope-bridge tolls of the treetop village and strung them in a net 40 feet up. Mr 6 talks it down with a riddle, and the net spills 1,260 amber beads onto the platform. Ormendale insists on keeping 25% of them as a 'thinking fee', and the rest is shared equally among the 9 bridge-keeper families.
question: How many amber beads does each family receive?
solution: Ormendale keeps 25% of 1260 = 315 beads, so 1260 − 315 = 945 beads are left to share.
praise: Dividing by the 9 families was the right instinct — the missing step was taking out Ormendale's 25% first.
hint: Find 25% of 1260 and subtract it before you split anything among the 9 families.
victory: Ormendale yawns, pleased with its fee, and the nine families cross home on bridges that no longer cost a thing. Mr 6 collects his payment in snacks.
imagePrompt: A shaggy sloth-like hoarder hanging from a rope bridge high in a misty forest canopy while a small numeral-six knight pours glowing amber beads into nine waiting baskets, soft green dappled light.
